newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee industry sees growth in Poland.
newsitem.headline: German coffee industry sees growth in Poland.

text.p: Coffee consumption in Poland was likely to expand although scattered retailing structures hampered distribution, Germany's coffee industry association DKV wrote in its quarterly newsletter.
"Poland is an interesting growth market because of population growth and strong underlying demand," DKV said, but it did not offer a market size forecast.
Poland's annual per-capita consumption had risen five-fold since 1989 to two kilos but by comparison Germany's was 6.9 kg, DKV said.
Coffee supplies were presently reaching the consumer relatively slowly and in small portions from numerous little shops, but sales should eventually benefit from improving wholesale patterns.
Poland imports around 100,000 tonnes of green coffee a year, mostly Indonesian and Vietnamese robustas.
In addition, it imports soluble coffees from Germany and directly from origin countries.
Suppliers of leading instant brands "Nescafe" and "Grandos," a German export product, complained about the damaging rise of imitation jars containing cheap, but substandard, products.
DKV also said an increasing share of Colombians in Poland's green coffee imports, mostly handled via German ports, was raising the relative share of arabicas.

Since Poland applied prohibitive import taxes on roasted coffee in 1993, western roasters started producing directly in the country and now have a 60 percent market share. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
